description:
FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-03) from the BB (#994) merge-review probe battery (scratchpad p994/tail.pl row `rgoto`).  PRE-EXISTING on main 605b837; NOT caused by #994 (the row is wrong with PCL_OPT=-tail-return too, and RIGHT with PCL_OPT=-insensitive-call).

REPRO:
    our @a = (7,8,9);
    sub ra    { return @a }
    sub rgoto { my $t = 0; goto &ra }
    print "@{[ rgoto() ]} / ", scalar(rgoto()), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3:  7 8 9 / 3
  PCL default:  3 / 3            <-- the list-context call answered the COUNT
  PCL_OPT=none: 7 8 9 / 3

MECHANISM (read off the emission): the call site is `(make-p-box (p-array-init (pl-rgoto)))` with NO `p-list-ctx` bind, because `_sub_return_facts` (the `insensitive-call` gate's oracle, ir-spec Â§4) answers "never observes *wantarray*" for rgoto -- its body has no `return` of a context-sensitive value and no wantarray read.  But `goto &ra` REPLACES the frame: ra runs in rgoto's CALLER's context, so rgoto's sensitivity is ra's (and for `goto &$coderef` it is UNKNOWN).  The facts walker must treat `goto &NAME` / `goto &$ref` / `goto &{...}` as a context-OBSERVING event (conservative: the sub is sensitive), exactly like a `return f()` of an unknown callee does.

FIX SHAPE: one arm in `_sub_return_facts`' body walk (rule 11: find where `return CALL` is already classified as sensitive and route `goto &...` through the same verdict; for a KNOWN target the target's own facts may be inherited -- second step, only if measured).  Guard: a row in the insensitive-call guard file (grep Pl/t for `insensitive-call`), list AND scalar spellings, inverse-verified.  Bars: Pl/ change -> corpus-diff (call sites that gain a bind), emission-ab, sweep, companion op/ (goto.t is TRANSPILE-FAIL today -- #993 phase 1 -- so it will not move yet).

RELATED: ir-spec Â§4 (context protocol) + Â§6.4 (goto), Pl/Passes.pm `insensitive-call`, #1022 (unlabelled last in a called sub -- a different frame question).

=== DONE (s470bi) ===
FIX: `Pl/Parser2.pm::_sub_return_facts`, the oracle behind the Kind-A
`insensitive-call` gate, walked `PPI::Statement::Break` nodes and looked only
at `return`.  A body whose exit is `goto &NAME` therefore looked like a body
with NO exits at all -- provably wantarray-insensitive -- and the call site
dropped its `p-list-ctx`/`p-scalar-ctx` bind, so the target ran in the AMBIENT
context.  A `goto` keyword now sets the verdict an unknown callee already gets
(`insensitive = 0`, family ''), routed through that same path rather than
invented (rule 11).

EVERY `goto` counts, not only the `&`-forms: `goto &NAME` / `goto &$ref` /
`goto &{...}` REPLACE the frame (the target runs in THIS sub's CALLER's
context, which is exactly why `p-goto-sub` restores `*wantarray*`), and
`goto LABEL` can land anywhere.  The change can only ever REMOVE a Kind-A
verdict.

TWO SILENT WRONGS, both now identical to perl 5.40.3 on the default emission
AND under PCL_OPT=none (scratch/s469bi/p1045/):
  "@{[ rgoto() ]}"   perl `7 8 9`   PCL was `3` (the COUNT)
  scalar(gw())       perl `S`       PCL was `L`
All three `&`-spellings covered.

BARS: corpus-diff 3 of 111 (args.t, sort.t -- new since #1035 prints the
verdict -- and state.t), silent drops unchanged; emission-ab over 1048 files
RCDIFF 0 with 14 of the DIFFs carrying a `goto` and every one read; gate green.
GUARDS: `Pl/t/goto-sub-phase-01.t` 17 -> 19 rows and `Pl/t/parser2-01.t` +2
(the second being the INVERSE: the same sub without the goto stays
insensitive).  Inverse-verified against main -- exactly those three rows fail
there.
subject: SILENT WRONG (Kind-A `insensitive-call`): a sub whose body ends in `goto &NAME` is classified wantarray-INSENSITIVE by Parser2::_sub_return_facts, so the CALL SITE omits the context bind and the goto TARGET runs in the wrong context -- `sub g { my $t = 0; goto &ra } my @x = g()` gets the COUNT (3) where perl gets the list (7 8 9); correct under PCL_OPT=none / -insensitive-call
